fields.v: Input: agent instruction file (Markdown). Generated: refined standalone constraints with header path and stable hash IDs; JSON file of executable Python checks in four domains: Process (PATH shell shims blocking prohibited commands), Source (Tree-sitter AST queries), Architectural-Deterministic (NetworkX dependency-graph checks), Architectural-Semantic (LLM-as-judge rubrics, warnings only). Violation traces returned to the agent

fields.v: Check generation: Markdown AST parse -> path-aware slicing -> LLM refinement of each constraint (gpt-5.2-chat) -> intent router to domain -> expert generators (Claude Code + Opus 4.5) with self-test loop, syntax check and dry run -> JSON of checks. Runtime enforcement: shims intercept commands; static/architectural checks on repo, diff or unstaged changes; violations fed back to the agent for self-correction (max 5 rounds in evaluation). Incremental re-generation when instruction file changes

fields.v:
Metrics: SWE-bench Lite resolution (official harness) and constraint compliance (ContextCov's executable oracle, post-hoc for baselines). The author states no success threshold, so no verdict is given. All with OpenCode + GPT-5.2 (critic for LLM Reflection: Claude Opus 4.5). Number of runs per task not stated
- Vanilla (AGENTS.md in context, no feedback) + OpenCode + GPT-5.2 (baseline): resolved 159/300 (53.0%); compliance 201 (67.0%); end-to-end mean 327.9 s (median 184.7). Quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: no criterion stated by the authors
- LLM Reflection + OpenCode + GPT-5.2 (critic Claude Opus 4.5): resolved 157 (52.3%); compliance 151 (50.3%); avg rounds 2.30, 85 hit the 5-round cap (28%); feedback 19,455 chars and 133.7 s mean; end-to-end mean 461.4 s (median 379.2). Quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: no criterion stated by the authors
- ContextCov + OpenCode + GPT-5.2: resolved 172 (57.3%); compliance 265 (88.3%); avg rounds 1.31, 29 hit cap (10%); feedback 6,292 chars and 27.7 s mean; end-to-end mean 422.4 s (median 240.0). Quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: no criterion stated by the authors

fields.v: Tasks: SWE-bench Lite (300), with AGENTS.md files generated by a few-shot LLM from existing repo docs, lint configs and CI files. Configurations: Vanilla, LLM Reflection, ContextCov. Baselines: Vanilla and LLM Reflection. Held constant: agent scaffold (OpenCode), coding model (GPT-5.2), instruction files, 5-round feedback budget for both feedback methods. Acceptance tests: official SWE-bench harness; compliance via ContextCov's own oracle (post-hoc for baselines). Repetitions: Not stated (one run per task apparently). Human intervention: none during runs

fields.v: Code and evaluation results: https://github.com/reSHARMA/ContextCov. Table 1 (per-repository) jumbled by pdftotext; totals rebuilt (1,498 lines, 665 segments, 241 source / 296 process / 158 arch-deterministic / 93 arch-semantic = 788 checks). Reporting inconsistencies: abstract claims '3.4x lower feedback cost', while the body gives ~3x lower feedback cost (19,455 vs 6,292 chars) and 3.4x higher cost-efficiency (p. 8); '780/781' Python checks parsed (p. 6) does not match 788 checks of which 93 are semantic rubrics, not Python; Figure 4 caption labels 'RQ5' and 'Self-Reflection' (= LLM Reflection). Compliance oracle is the proposed tool itself applied post-hoc to baselines. Motivating scenarios based on informal probing. No pre-registration. Programming language: Python (tasks); tool in Python, Tree-sitter grammars for Python, TS, JS, Go, Rust
